stories.title: Jensen Huang had a strict no one-on-one meetings rule for his 60 direct reports—and Nvidia’s interim CEO has a similar mantra: ‘We don’t waste a dime’
stories.summary: Nvidia’s ex-CEO Jensen Huang said frequent meetings cluttered his schedule—and interim CEO Colette Kress is just as obsessed with speed.

sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Jensen Huang had a strict no one-on-one meetings rule for his 60 direct reports—and Nvidia’s interim CEO has a similar mantra: ‘We don’t waste a dime’
sources.text: Former Nvidia CEO and cofounder Jensen Huang famously avoided unnecessary meetings, prioritizing efficiency over routine check-ins. Even with, at one point, 60 direct reports , he refused to do catch-ups. Now that he’s resigned , the question is whether his successor (currently Colette Kress who has stepped up on an interim basis) will keep the rule. Speaking at Stanford University , Huang once disclosed his aversion to frequent catch-ups. “I don’t do one-on-ones with any of them,” he said. Huang argued frequent meetings would clutter his schedule. He said they would also get in the way of the broader team’s ability to address challenges, work effectively, and stay transparent. “They never hear me say something to them, that is only for them to know,” he said. “There’s not one piece of information that I somehow secretly tell the staff; I don’t tell the rest of the company.” “In that way, our company was designed for agility. For information to be to flow as quickly as possible. For people to be empowered by what they are able to do, not what they know,” he added. But that doesn’t mean he had no time for his team. Huang insisted he still regularly caught up with his executives. They just didn’t need to set time aside in their diaries to be on the same page. “I write no reviews for any of them,” he added. “I give them constant reviews and they provide the same to me.” And when an employee genuinely needed a moment of his time, Huang insisted he’d “drop everything for them.” Stepping into Huang’s shoes (for now) is CFO Colette Kress . The interim CEO, who has an estimated net worth of $1.2 billion according to Forbes , holds a bachelor’s in finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University. After nearly three decades’ worth of financial roles at companies such as Texas Instruments , Cisco, and Microsoft , she joined Nvidia in September 2013. Since then, she guided the company’s finances through a significant transformation, from a business largely focused on video game hardware to a chipmaking powerhouse at the center of the AI boom—and watched its market cap soar from about $9 billion to, at its peak, $5 trillion. Its since dropped below $4 trillion upon the news regarding Huang. She hasn’t revealed whether she’ll ditch one-on-ones too. But the 59-year-old, who has spent 13 years as Huang’s right hand on Nvidia’s finances, seems to share his affinity for efficiency. “We do not waste a day, we don’t waste a dime,” Kress said in 2024. “And those two things are really important about us, our agility to move fast, but our ability to not waste things along the way.” Huang isn’t the first leader to argue that meetings aren’t the best use of time. Pandora’s former CEO Alexander Lacik told Fortune too many meetings result in every department or company issue getting “equal attention”—whether or not it needs it. He limited his catch-ups with management. “There’s only one, two, three activities that actually draw disproportionate value and the rest is just background noise,” he said. “As time has gone by and I’m getting towards the end of my career, I’m much more clear on trying to insert myself where I make a high impact.” United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby caps his meetings at four hours a day , and wants the ones he does attend to be “quick” and “almost all conversational.” E-commerce giant Shopify took one step further and actually axed all meetings involving more than two people in 2023, in a company-wide “calendar purge” meant to give employees more time to work on other tasks. And even Amazon founder Jeff Bezos—a big fan of “ messy meetings ”—mandates a strict protocol to ensure they’re actually useful, complete with a six-page memo instead of a PowerPoint (because they’re too vague) and half an hour set aside at the start of the meeting to silently read it together before having “a really elevated discussion.” A version of this story was published on Fortune.com on June 12, 2024.

sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure shakes AI industry’s foundations
sources.text: Honeypot or not, the Chinese executive/accused spy with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair this week should have been a flashing red light to him. So should fraternizing with one of your own VPs — and reportedly another employee too! In the end, all that, and maybe more to come, was just too much for Nvidia’s board to bear despite the commanding position Huang (pictured) held not only at Nvidia but in the entire artificial intelligence industry. Indeed, the speed with which he resigned — spectacularly stupid as his behavior was — still makes me wonder if there are other shoes to drop, especially on the legal or national security fronts. Market researcher SemiAnalysis thinks it came down to pressure from the U.S. intelligence community that’s very unhappy Nvidia chips have apparently been smuggled to China. Huang was something of an AI puppet master, providing the chips and software to power the entire industry as well as seemingly unlimited cash to fund and backstop everyone from AI leaders such as OpenAI and Anthropic to innumerable cloud compute providers worldwide. No single person inside or outside Nvidia seems likely to fill that role. However, Nvidia really is much more than Jensen Huang. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress helped craft the financial arrangements that in part put Nvidia at the center of AI — though for what it’s worth, Huang himself wasn’t a fan lately . Some of his direct reports such as high-performance computing chief Ian Buck seem quite capable of carrying on, if perhaps not with Huang’s panache. One company is never one person, and shouldn’t be. I expect a less centralized Nvidia going forward, whoever’s at the top. More than that, AI is much more than Jensen Huang, and it will continue to be going forward. It’s easy to forget that although Huang brilliantly helped create this new wave, AI and its enablers also are what made him a rock star. But that time is now over. Nvidia and certainly the AI industry shouldn’t be depending on one person to keep everything afloat anyway. The reverberations of his sudden and shocking departure will continue to echo for a long time to come across Nvidia, its investors watching hundreds of billions of market cap evaporate, legions of Jensen fanboys and the entire artificial intelligence ecosystem. A lot of people are hoping desperately that he didn’t just pop the AI bubble (though others are thinking he did). It seems unlikely this will be the pin, but we’re dealing with a lot of unlikely things in the past week or so, for better and worse, and this shock is clearly rattling the foundations. All that managed to overshadow what otherwise would be the big news this week: Anthropic went on the road to pitch its initial public offering . It’s hoping to raise more than $64 billion and keep the AI trade humming in Nvidia’s near-term absence. Looks like next Thursday is the big day. And it’s not the only good news in AI — that is, if the IPO is successful. After a difficult month on the stock front, uber neocloud CoreWeave provided a pleasant AI surprise with upside earnings and guidance, lifting its shares almost 25% Wednesday. AI chipmaker Cerebras’ shares rose almost 18% in late trading Thursday on positive guidance and a Microsoft deal . Cisco Systems said demand is strong for AI infrastructure, even if investors shrugged, and chipmaking equipment supplier Applied Materials said AI boosted demand as well. Not everyone fared so well, though. Dutch neocloud Nebius saw its shares drop almost 17% Thursday as it lowered its outlook despite close to sevenfold revenue growth in the last quarter. The stock drop no doubt was partly because of Nvidia, which is, of course, an investor. CoreWeave –yes, another Nvidia investment — lost 7% Thursday. Couple of really big outages out there: first, Microsoft Outlook , grounding a lot of office workers, then the whole damn U.S. air traffic control system , grounding thousands of flights. Sovereignty is on many enterprise buyers’ lips these days, the notion that enterprises need a way to assert more control over their technology estates and protect their customers’ data. TheCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and Amit Eyal Govrin just completed the first of a series of reports on how to approach sovereignty, this one focused on the hyperscale cloud providers. The software orchestrator Kubernetes has become boring, but as SiliconANGLE’s John Furrier said at this week’s KubeCon in Salt Lake City, that means it’s a success — with lessons for AI developers. “A lot of things that are happening in cloud-native that were involved in microservices in Kubernetes world are actually the same challenges in the AI world,” he noted. IBM has been working hard on quantum computing for a long time now, but at its Quantum Developer Conference in Chicago this week, it showed significant progress, according to Dave Vellante. Its goal now is to show actual industry impact by 2028, a laudable goal that presents a lot of challenges, Dave wrote in his Special Breaking Analysis this week. Next week the SC26 high-performance computing conference comes to Chicago, and theCUBE and theCUBE Research will be onsite with interviews and analysis. There’s also Microsoft Ignite in San Francisco. And earnings next week include… Nvidia! Bring the popcorn. Here’s all of this week’s enterprise and emerging tech news, most of it not salacious, along with analysis and commentary from SiliconANGLE and beyond: Breaking Analysis: Sovereign or not? The 2026 Hyperscaler Buyer’s Guide Breaking Analysis: AI cyber resilience and the trust gap Dario goes overboard with AI claims ahead of Anthropic’s IPO — the same guy who says AI could also extinguish us. Somebody give him back his Xanax! Also, I really don’t think mental illness is a compute problem. sources.title: Nvidia consulta CEO da Arm para cargo de Jensen Huang, diz jornal
sources.text: A Nvidia já tem ao menos uma pessoa em mente para o cargo de CEO após a renúncia de Jensen Huang. De acordo com o Financial Times , o nome de Rene Haas surge como candidato em potencial, embora nenhuma decisão tenha sido tomada por enquanto. O executivo é CEO da empresa britânica de semicondutores Arm , especializada em montar projetos de arquitetura de chips para outras empresas. Haas ocupa o cargo desde fevereiro de 2022. A atual empresa mais valiosa do mundo está sem gerente executivo fixo desde quinta-feira (12) , quando Huang renunciou após a divulgação de dois casos extraconjugais mantidos pelo executivo. Atualmente, a marca é comandada por uma CEO interina, Colette Kress , que também é CFO da Nvidia. Até agora, nomes externos não haviam sido considerados e até mesmo executivos da Nvidia eram pouco especulados como sucessores — Huang era um dos cofundadores da marca e ocupava de forma estável o cargo de gerência executiva desde 1993. Nvidia e Arm foram procuradas pela reportagem original, mas não se manifestaram sobre o assunto. À CNBC , a Nvidia afirmou que está “em processo de seleção de uma empresa de recrutamento para o cargo de CEO” e negou que tenha entrado “em contato com nenhum candidato em potencial” . Haas já tem familiaridade com a Nvidia por mais de um motivo. Ele trabalhou na companhia ao longo de sete anos na década de 2000 , chegando ao cargo de vice-presidente e gerente geral da divisão de computação. Em 2013, o executivo trocou a companhia pela rival Arm. Curiosamente, a trajetória de ambas as empresas quase se juntou tempos depois: em 2021, a Nvidia chegou a anunciar a aquisição da Arm por US$ 40 bilhões. Porém, a negociação foi desfeita em fevereiro do ano seguinte , após a dupla não conseguir a aprovação de órgãos reguladores. A compra recebeu pressão inclusive de fabricantes de eletrônicos, que temiam que a fusão prejudicasse a concorrência no mercado. A Arm seguiu independente e realizou a oferta pública de ações em 2023. A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? sources.title: Jensen Huang and the decline of the visionary showman founder CEO
sources.text: The Steve Jobs of GPUs has been shown the door.﻿ On January 6th, 2025, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang got his rockstar moment at last. He strode triumphantly onstage, hand raised in the air, to the claps and cheers of a 14,000-person arena absolutely packed with influencers and fans, their faces awash in blue glow, as he made his entrance in a black leather jacket that shimmered in the stadium’s lights. Few are cheering for Jensen Huang now. He has left Nvidia after seemingly enabling two chip smuggling scandals and allegedly having three extramarital affairs , including one with an alleged Chinese spy at the same time he was mingling with President Donald Trump. The world is watching to see if this scandal might disrupt the entire US AI industry and perhaps destabilize the stock market along with it. That’s because Huang wasn’t merely running the first $5 trillion company , he was the visionary leader in control of the must-have GPUs powering the worldwide AI boom, part of a company that represents around 6 percent of the S&P 500 stock market index all by itself. And he didn’t plan for succession if he ever stepped down. The 63-year-old once said he preferred to die on the job ; he once suggested he’d work until he was 90 or 100 , then carry on leading the company as a robot. It’s not easy to replace Huang, partly because he had no deputies. Around 60 employees reported directly to the CEO . “He built the company around himself, and everything that happened there flowed through him,” says IDC analyst and former computing journalist Tom Mainelli. “Jensen is Nvidia, and Nvidia is Jensen,” Jon Peddie, a computer industry analyst who’s been tracking Nvidia since its inception, tells me. But Nvidia isn’t Jensen anymore. He has left the company he cofounded 33 years ago. It’s the end of an era, and not just for Nvidia — because Jensen Huang was Big Tech’s last true example of a visionary showman founder CEO. “He was both the visionary and the tactical leader, the closest thing tech has had to Steve Jobs,” Moor Insights & Strategy chief analyst Pat Moorhead tells me. Elon Musk didn’t exactly found Tesla and has quite the track record of broken promises, and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg has proven to be neither visionary nor showman so far. Google’s Larry Page and Sergey Brin stepped away in 2019 as their company dealt with growing employee turmoil , leaving the company in the hands of Sundar Pichai, and both Microsoft and Apple have each passed the torch twice since the days of Bill Gates and Steve Jobs. Some say Apple’s Steve Jobs broke the CEO mold, but he created a mold of his own. Huang was one of countless tech leaders who followed his example by introducing their products in keynote speeches, adopting a single recognizable piece of clothing like Jobs’ trademark black turtleneck, and even occasionally teasing “one more thing” for the surprise at the end of their presentations. In the newsroom, we’d sometimes joke about the Jobs wannabes; many were stiff suits who didn’t have the credibility to pull it off. I thought Huang might be a Jobs wannabe, too, the first time I saw that he’d adopted a black jacket as his uniform. (It was not always a leather jacket; an earlier version was a Nvidia-branded softshell.) Huang later insisted on wearing a jacket even when the temperature was hot — more than once, I saw him sweat profusely rather than take it off. Unlike Jobs, he also held quite a few keynotes when he didn’t have much news to share; he liked to repeat the company’s previous accomplishments as if they were brand-new. But even if Huang didn’t have the same gravitas as Jobs, he did have exciting tech up his sleeves and loved to demo it onstage. He knew how to get people excited about the future of visual computing with eye-opening gaming graphics, physics and lighting demos, and eventually image recognition, AI weather simulations, digital copies of real-world factories, and the robots that can virtually train in them. His Nvidia tried to educate people about the how and why of GPUs, too; I still remember in 2008 when Nvidia invited the Mythbusters to demo the difference between serial processing and parallel processing by firing a 1,100-nozzle paintball gun to “paint” the Mona Lisa in one shot. What I didn’t know back then: Huang was a visionary founder. He took Nvidia to fame and fortune through a series of tremendous bets. In 1996, three years after he cofounded the company at a Denny’s diner, Nvidia nearly went out of business while working on a failed graphics chip for the Sega Dreamcast game console. But even though he didn’t deliver that chip, Huang personally convinced Sega to invest $5 million afterward, The Wall Street Journal reported in 2024. He then turned around and bet the company again on the Riva 128 PC graphics accelerator, an effort so ambitious he had to lay off over half of Nvidia’s roughly 100 staffers, skip the prototyping stage, and rush it straight to production, and he still only had one month of payroll left by the time it shipped, The New Yorker wrote in 2023. Thankfully, it was a success, selling a million units in just four months and paving the way for both the GeForce GPU and a long-term relationship with chip fabricator TSMC. Roughly eight years later, Huang decided it wasn’t enough to be the leader in PC gaming graphics alone. He bet the company’s entire gross profit , he told podcaster Lex Fridman, on shipping a new feature inside those graphics cards that no one had asked for: CUDA. It was the ability to use a GPU for other kinds of computing tasks beyond graphics, and Huang said it increased the cost of every GeForce graphics card by 50 percent. “Originally there was no market or market demand for it. It was almost as if they built it because they could,” says Peddie. “Jensen had the vision for what it could be and the courage to pursue it in spite of the opinions of others.” “NVIDIA was effectively investing in a computing platform that extended far beyond graphics,

sources.title: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s exit
sources.text: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has drawn a range of responses across Asia, with some governments moving to confirm chip supply commitments, while others are monitoring the impact on local projects or addressing ongoing investigations. On Sunday, November 8, Nvidia’s board launched an independent investigation after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation; Huang admitted to an affair with Alice Huang, a former executive at Singapore-based chip company Megaspeed. Nvidia’s influence extends far beyond the United States. The chip giant has built close ties with companies worldwide, particularly in Asia, where many of its key partners play important roles in the global AI industry. China’s foreign ministry rejected allegations on November 10 that a Chinese businesswoman linked to former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang was a spy, calling them groundless and a smear against Beijing. On Friday , a spokesperson reiterated opposition to export controls that disrupt global supply chains and stated the ministry was not aware of reports linking restricted Nvidia chips to a Shanghai data center associated with Alice Huang. Huang’s exit has also raised uncertainty over more than $3 billion in Chinese AI computing projects reliant on Nvidia’s restricted processors, according to Reuters’ review of procurement notices, investment plans and corporate disclosures. Many of these chips are subject to U.S. export controls, making them difficult for Chinese companies to obtain. In Singapore, authorities seized the passport of Alice Huang, former CEO of Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, in June 2025 as part of an investigation into possible false declarations regarding server purchases, according to the Ministry of Home Affairs. The Singapore ministry said police took her passport to ensure she remained available for questioning, as she was not based in Singapore. The investigation examined whether servers shipped from Singapore to Malaysia were later sent to other countries without proper declaration. In February 2026, police found insufficient evidence to establish that Alice Huang had committed offenses related to the suspected false declarations, according to the ministry. However, authorities said she had knowingly provided inaccurate information about her role at Megaspeed. She was issued a warning and barred from re-entering Singapore. Her passport was returned that month. Singapore also said it received limited assistance from U.S. authorities despite repeated requests for information about U.S. server maker Supermicro. Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs said its investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals remains ongoing. The ministry did not identify the six individuals or specify their alleged roles in the case. South Korea has close ties to Nvidia, with major chipmakers Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix playing important roles in supplying memory chips used in its AI processors. Following Huang’s exit, South Korea’s Science Ministry said Nvidia had reaffirmed its plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs to the country and to continue joint AI projects. Apart from that, South Korea’s government AI strategy council held an emergency meeting on Friday to assess the potential impact of Huang’s departure on the country’s AI industry, per a local media report. Taiwan’s Economy Minister Kung Ming-shin said Huang’s departure was unlikely to significantly change the growth of the global AI industry, according to local media . Meanwhile, Taipei’s city government said Nvidia’s planned overseas headquarters in the city remained on track despite the leadership change. The company has met its contractual obligations so far, and officials said they would continue to support the project. In Japan, the Industry Ministry said the government would closely monitor Nvidia following Huang’s resignation, describing the chipmaker as an important player in Japan’s AI semiconductor industry, Reuters reported. Deputy chief cabinet secretary Masanao Ozaki said it was too early to assess the impact on the global AI industry, while stressing Japan’s commitment to ensuring a stable supply of semiconductors. sources.title: Nvidia scandal draws in Commerce Secretary Lutnick, who reportedly agrees to testify about China chip sales
sources.text: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee, as the fallout from ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy intensifies. Lutnick was summoned by Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott amid scrutiny over whether Nvidia could have supplied advanced artificial intelligence chips to Chinese companies and thereby potentially threatened U.S. national security. Huang and Lutnick both received letters on Thursday evening requesting them to testify in separate hearings on Dec. 3 and Dec. 10, respectively. The letter to Lutnick asked the commerce secretary to testify regarding "recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns." "Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions," Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News on Thursday. CNBC contacted the Commerce Department for comment. The letter to Huang said that reports about his relationship with the alleged Chinese spy "raise significant national security concerns." Huang has acknowledged an affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that has bought over $4.8 billion of advanced Nvidia AI chips over the past two years. The scandal, in addition to reports of a separate affair with a senior executive at Nvidia, led to his resignation on Thursday. There is growing bipartisan scrutiny of the Commerce Department Secretary's approach to chip policy and whether his department was doing enough to restrict the supply of AI chips to China. Lawmakers are also questioning whether the department was overseeing Nvidia's exports thoroughly enough Senator Jim Banks has been particularly scathing, saying Lutnick "appears to have used loopholes to allow some of these chip sales to occur," in an appearance on Fox News on Thursday. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass, who will chair the Senate Banking Committee from January, said on Thursday "Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military." In a joint letter with incoming Senate Foreign Relations Chair Chris Coons published Wednesday, they said all documents relating to the export of Nvidia chips to China must be preserved. Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore. and Rep. Richard E. Neal, D-Mass. told Lutnick they were investigating the approval of sales of Nvidia chips to companies with links to the Chinese government, military and sanctioned entities. Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla. said on Thursday that Congress needed to investigate the role of the Commerce Department in approving the export to China of AI chips, but added that he had confidence in Lutnick. Criticism is mounting on President Donald Trump 's administration for declining to include over 100 companies highlighted as national security risks on a trade blacklist, including China's AI startup DeepSeek and memory chipmaker CXMT, Reuters reported in June. Lutnick is a long-standing friend of Trump, with their relationship spanning over three decades, and is widely regarded as a close confidant of the President.

sources.title: Lutnick faces questions over Nvidia spy scandal. His sons' firm has deep ties to the chipmaker
sources.text: In late September, Cantor Fitzgerald hosted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and other top executives from the chipmaker for investor meetings in New York, according to a Cantor research report reviewed by CNBC. The Wall Street firm liked what it heard. "We continue to view NVDA as the best risk/reward in our coverage," Cantor analyst C.J. Muse and his colleagues wrote in a research report dated Oct. 3 that maintained a $350 price target and overweight rating on the stock. Yet the firm, formerly run by Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and now led by his sons, Brandon and Kyle, reported a nearly 50% decline in the number of Nvidia shares it held between September 2025 and March 2026 , according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings that excludes options. Nvidia had been one of the largest stock positions reported in Cantor's filings. The decline coincided with White House and U.S. intelligence officials pressing Lutnick to crack down on Megaspeed , a Singapore-based company suspected of funneling Nvidia's advanced artificial intelligence chips to China . Lutnick repeatedly resisted those efforts, Axios reported Nov. 11. By the time Cantor hosted Huang in New York, Lutnick had also received a classified intelligence warning, according to a Nov. 10 Axios report, about Huang's ties to a suspected Chinese spy and had appeared alongside the CEO at a G20 technology summit in North Carolina. Even as Cantor pared back its Nvidia stake, it continued doing business across the chipmaker's AI empire. A CNBC review of securities filings, corporate announcements and Wall Street research found the firm has helped arrange billions of dollars in financing for Nvidia's business partners while maintaining close ties to the chipmaker's leadership. Those ties have drawn fresh scrutiny following Huang's resignation Thursday and Axios' reporting that Lutnick repeatedly resisted a crackdown on companies suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, despite President Donald Trump authorizing new export restrictions on those companies for a third time on Nov. 5. An ethics expert said the relationship between Lutnick and his former firm's investments may raise questions, given what the secretary knew about Nvidia. Richard Painter , the former chief White House ethics lawyer for President George W. Bush and now a corporate law professor at the University of Minnesota, said that while "there's no proof of" Lutnick sharing nonpublic information with Cantor Fitzgerald, "the appearance doesn't look great." "His conversations with his sons better be about publicly available information," Painter told CNBC. There is no evidence that Lutnick's sons had advance knowledge of the intelligence concerns, that changes in Cantor's reported holdings were tied to any warnings or that the firm's business interests influenced their father's decisions. "Cantor has to date from time to time had only immaterial stand-alone proprietary positions in Nvidia, unlike the positions reflected in 13F filings which were entered into in the ordinary course of business in connection with client swap transactions, that are common in institutional markets," a Cantor spokesperson told CNBC. Cantor declined to answer CNBC's other questions. The Commerce Department, the White House, Howard Lutnick, Brandon Lutnick and Kyle Lutnick did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment or detailed questions about the findings. As scrutiny of Huang intensified, Cantor Chairman Brandon Lutnick was publicly praising the chipmaker's leadership. "Nvidia is one of the great companies on the planet, and they have an amazing leadership team," Brandon Lutnick told Fox Business on Wednesday. Trump is standing by Howard Lutnick. A White House official told Reuters on Thursday that the president maintains "complete confidence" in the commerce secretary. But cracks in the administration's unity emerged Friday, when Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC's "Squawk Box" that the departments of Treasury, Defense and State and the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative all "were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the entity list for months." Bessent pointed to Commerce as the department responsible for imposing the entity list, which identifies restricted businesses and other groups, adding, "You will have to ask them about their internal processes." Nvidia was Cantor's second-largest reported stock position before Howard Lutnick left Wall Street to become commerce secretary in February 2025, behind only bitcoin investor MicroStrategy, now known as Strategy . At the end of 2024, the firm disclosed more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares worth $479 million, according to its quarterly securities filing . That share count held steady through September 2025, but its value climbed 36% to $652 million, according to Cantor's quarterly securities filing , as the Trump administration moved over the summer to ease restrictions on Nvidia's H20 chip sales to China . Over the following six months, however, the number of Nvidia shares Cantor reported holding fell by 49%, to 3 million in December and 1.78 million by the end of March 2026 , with their value dropping from $652 million to $310 million, according to a CNBC analysis of securities filings. Pressure on Howard Lutnick was also mounting on Capitol Hill. Sens. Jim Banks, R-Ind., and Elizabeth Warren , D-Mass., in March urged the secretary to suspend or reconsider Nvidia's export licenses after three people linked to Nvidia customer Super Micro Computer were indicted on charges of conspiring to smuggle AI chips to China. "The Trump administration, I think, leaks like a sieve when it comes to nonpublic government information getting to various hedge fund guys," Painter said, though he stressed there is no evidence Howard Lutnick had shared such information with his sons. sources.name: Olhar Digital IA
sources.title: Você confia? Agente de IA da OpenAI, ChatGPT Wallet fará compras pelo usuário e promete segurança
sources.text: A OpenAI anunciou nesta sexta-feira (13) o lançamento da ChatGPT Wallet. A novidade permite que agentes de inteligência artificial paguem por compras sem acessar os dados do cartão do usuário. Segundo a desenvolvedora, o sistema pede uma verificação de segurança obrigatória para cada transação. Ainda de acordo com a startup, a carteira digital foi desenvolvida em parceria com grandes empresas do setor de meios de pagamento, como Visa, Mastercard e American Express. “Apresentamos a ChatGPT Wallet, que eleva o padrão para pagamentos seguros por agentes. É a primeira carteira digital que permite que os agentes paguem sem acesso aos dados reais do cartão do usuário e que exige uma verificação de segurança para cada compra, preservando os benefícios e proteções existentes do cartão para contestações elegíveis” – diz a OpenAI, em comunicado . Mas a nova ferramenta não chega para todo mundo neste primeiro momento: por enquanto, estará disponível nos Estados Unidos para assinantes do ChatGPT Pro com 18 anos ou mais e que possuam cartões emitidos no país. O acesso será feito por meio dos “dots”, os agentes de IA sempre ativos da empresa. “ 1,2 bilhão de pessoas usam o ChatGPT semanalmente, e muitas delas o utilizam para pesquisar produtos, comparar opções e decidir o que comprar. Com a Carteira ChatGPT, agora estamos ajudando as pessoas a concluir compras e oferecendo aos seus agentes uma forma de pagamento que as empresas podem aceitar com seus sistemas existentes” – afirma a OpenAI. Os usuários podem revisar os itens, o total e o cartão selecionado antes de cada compra. Em seguida, basta aprová-la com uma verificação de segurança – seja reconhecimento facial ou leitura de impressão digital. A rede de pagamentos fornecerá um token de pagamento em vez dos dados reais do cartão. Em outras palavras: nem a empresa nem o agente poderão vê-los, diz a OpenAI. “Para aceitar pagamentos da Carteira ChatGPT, os sites precisam garantir que os agentes não sejam bloqueados inadvertidamente, e os sistemas de pagamento e risco precisam reconhecer compras legítimas feitas pelos agentes (…) Com o tempo, esperamos que os usuários possam delegar as compras inteiramente ao seu agente, definindo parâmetros claros — como limites de gastos, categorias de compras ou períodos de tempo — e pré-aprovando essas compras com salvaguardas aprimoradas que se baseiam nas proteções atuais, incluindo verificações biométricas e registros claros de autorização” – conclui a startup. Bruno Capozzi é jornalista, mestre em Ciências Sociais e editor executivo do OD.

sources.name: Computer Hoy
sources.title: OpenAI estrena ChatGPT Wallet para que sus agentes de IA puedan realizar compras por ti
sources.text: Elígenos como tu fuente preferida en Google. OpenAI lanza ChatGPT Wallet en Estados Unidos para que los agentes Dots puedan ayudar en compras online con tarjetas Visa, Mastercard y American Express. OpenAI quiere que sus agentes de inteligencia artificial participen cada vez más en tareas cotidianas, y las compras son el siguiente paso. La compañía ha anunciado ChatGPT Wallet , una nueva cartera digital que permite a los agentes Dots gestionar adquisiciones en nombre de los usuarios utilizando tarjetas de pago registradas previamente. Por ahora, la función está limitada a suscriptores de ChatGPT Pro residentes en Estados Unidos y requiere una tarjeta Visa, Mastercard o American Express emitida en ese país. Sin embargo, el lanzamiento deja entrever la dirección que pretende seguir OpenAI, ya que la empresa aspira a que sus agentes asuman progresivamente más tareas relacionadas con el comercio electrónico. La nueva herramienta actúa como un intermediario entre la tarjeta bancaria del usuario y el comercio . En lugar de compartir directamente los datos de la tarjeta durante la compra, ChatGPT Wallet utiliza un token de pago para completar la operación, una técnica que busca reducir la exposición de información sensible. El proceso actual mantiene al usuario en el centro de la decisión. Los agentes Dots pueden ayudar a localizar productos, preparar la compra y gestionar distintos pasos del proceso, pero la aprobación final sigue dependiendo de la persona . Antes de completar una transacción, el usuario puede revisar los artículos seleccionados, comprobar el importe total, elegir la tarjeta que desea utilizar y validar la operación mediante un sistema de seguridad como reconocimiento facial o huella dactilar. OpenAI asegura que las recompensas asociadas a las tarjetas seguirán funcionando con normalidad y que las protecciones habituales frente a disputas continuarán aplicándose cuando corresponda. Además, cada compra genera un registro que permite consultar posteriormente la autorización realizada. Aunque el sistema exige actualmente una confirmación manual, la compañía ya ha adelantado cuál es su objetivo a largo plazo. OpenAI espera que en el futuro los usuarios puedan delegar determinadas compras de forma más amplia mediante reglas predefinidas, como límites de gasto, categorías concretas de productos o periodos determinados. Aun así, la empresa afirma que estos escenarios irán acompañados de medidas de protección adicionales. El lanzamiento también se produce en un momento en el que el acceso de los agentes de IA a plataformas comerciales se ha convertido en un tema cada vez más controvertido. Algunas empresas han comenzado a limitar o bloquear este tipo de herramientas para evitar que naveguen o realicen compras automáticamente en sus servicios. Por ahora, ChatGPT Wallet está disponible exclusivamente para clientes de ChatGPT Pro en Estados Unidos con tarjetas emitidas en ese mercado . No obstante, el lanzamiento supone un primer despliegue de una tecnología que podría extenderse a otros países y mercados en el futuro, aunque OpenAI no ha anunciado todavía planes concretos ni fechas para una expansión internacional.

sources.name: Canaltech
sources.title: Google lança modelo de IA veloz e eficiente; conheça o Gemini 4 Hydrogen
sources.text: O Google anunciou o Gemini 4 Hydrogen , novo modelo de inteligência artificial desenvolvido para acelerar tarefas de programação e fluxos de trabalho executados por agentes de IA. Com foco em velocidade e eficiência, ele pode funcionar sozinho ou em conjunto com o Gemini 4 Carbon e o Gemini 4 Argon, modelos focados em atividades que exigem raciocínio mais complexo e de longo prazo. Segundo Koray Kavukcuoglu, vice-presidente sênior do Google DeepMind e arquiteto-chefe de IA do Google, o Hydrogen assume tarefas que precisam de execução rápida , e o Carbon e Argon cuidam das demandas mais complexas. No Google Antigravity, o recurso Orchestrator gerencia essa divisão e alterna entre os modelos durante uma mesma sessão. Em testes com o Terminal-Bench 4.0, o sistema alcançou resultados próximos aos do Carbon, com 24% menos consumo de cota e conclusão das tarefas 19% mais rápida. O Carbon também pode coordenar vários agentes Hydrogen, responsáveis pela execução e verificação de alterações em ambientes isolados. O Hydrogen oferece quatro níveis de raciocínio (low, medium, high e xhigh), que definem a quantidade de processamento dedicada a cada tarefa. No Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, marcou 51 pontos no nível high, acima dos 50 do Argon, e chegou a 54 pontos no xhigh. Na configuração padrão (high), é 2,5 vezes mais rápido que o Gemini 3.8 Flash. O desempenho em programação também melhorou: o modelo alcançou 57% de sucesso no Terminal-Bench 4.1, contra 18,2% da versão anterior, e reduziu em mais de cinco vezes a ocorrência de respostas com informações inventadas. Com janela de contexto de até 1 milhão de tokens de entrada e 1 milhão de tokens de saída , o modelo processa PDFs, planilhas, áudios e vídeos. Também extrai informações de arquivos enviados e serviços conectados, como Gmail, Google Drive, Airtable e Dropbox. No aplicativo Gemini, aciona ferramentas e habilidades adequadas com mais frequência e segue instruções de tom e formato ao longo de conversas com várias interações. O Google também destaca melhorias de segurança . Em comparação com o Gemini 3.8 Flash, o Hydrogen reduziu em até 81% as ações que ultrapassam as instruções recebidas e em até 79% as tarefas executadas abaixo do esperado. A ocorrência de ações desalinhadas com os objetivos caiu 12 vezes. Segundo o Google, 99,9% do processo de raciocínio do modelo é legível. Uma auditoria com mais de 200 mil interações também confirmou que não houve edições enganosas na cadeia de raciocínio . O Hydrogen ainda demonstrou ser mais de 2,3 vezes mais resistente a ataques de injeção indireta de comandos no benchmark Gray Swan IPI. No HealthBench Pro, menos de 0,4% das perguntas médicas e científicas receberam recusas indevidas. O lançamento também inclui mudanças na Busca do Google , disponível globalmente. A ferramenta ganha respostas mais visuais, aprimoramento de consultas para encontrar mais links relacionados e melhor interpretação de perguntas com várias partes, erros de digitação e solicitações específicas. No Google Sheets, o Gemini gera modelos financeiros interativos mais de 30% mais rápido que os modelos anteriores. Os resultados aparecem no canvas da ferramenta e se ajustam a diferentes cenários de previsão. O recurso está disponível a partir dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra, incluindo assinaturas corporativas elegíveis. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen está disponível no aplicativo Gemini e na Busca do Google . No plano gratuito, o aplicativo seleciona o modelo automaticamente, de acordo com a solicitação. Nos planos pagos, o modelo pode ser escolhido no seletor de modelos. Já a integração com o Google Sheets atende aos assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra. Já os desenvolvedores podem utilizar o modelo pela API Gemini, no Google AI Studio e no Android Studio . Os assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e Ultra também encontram a novidade no Google Antigravity. O preço da API é de US$ 1,50 por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 7,50 por milhão de tokens de saída. No ambiente corporativo, o Hydrogen está disponível no Gemini para Empresas , tanto pela API quanto pelo seletor de modelos. A ferramenta também chegou ao Google Antigravity e ao Gemini para Google Sheets, neste último caso para assinaturas corporativas elegíveis. Se você gostou do conteúdo, talvez também se interesse por conferir “ 8 formas de assinar o Gemini mais barato ou de graça ”.

sources.name: Tecmundo
sources.title: Google lança Gemini 4 Hydrogen, IA intermediária e disponível para todos
sources.text: O Google anunciou o Gemini 4 Hydrogen, novo grande modelo de linguagem (LLM) de nível intermediário. A inteligência artificial foi desenvolvida para entregar resultados com agilidade e eficiência, sendo indicada para tarefas cotidianas e fluxos de trabalho agênticos. O modelo está disponível em diferentes níveis de acesso ao Gemini , incluindo opções gratuitas e pagas. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen segue o padrão de nomenclatura baseado em elementos da tabela periódica , ao lado das IAs de fronteira Gemini 4 Carbon e Gemini 4 Argon . Porém, diferentemente dos demais, o Hydrogen não é uma variante de altíssima performance, mas uma opção pensada para atender a mais usuários e demandas em maior escala. Assim, o Gemini 4 Hydrogen é mais apropriado para tarefas cotidianas que não exigem raciocínio tão amplo ou elaborado quanto o oferecido pelos modelos mais avançados. Para complementar o lançamento, o Google apresentou o Orchestrator (“Orquestrador”, em português) dentro do Google Antigravity . A ferramenta alterna entre modelos como Carbon e Hydrogen durante uma mesma sessão, escolhendo a melhor opção conforme a complexidade da tarefa — o Carbon atua mais como coordenador, enquanto o Hydrogen é incorporado a agentes responsáveis por atividades mais objetivas. Segundo o Google, o Orchestrator alcançou uma taxa de sucesso próxima à do Gemini 4 Carbon no Terminal-Bench 4.0, mas consumiu 24% menos da cota de uso e concluiu as tarefas 19% mais rápido. Nos testes de benchmark, o Google comparou os resultados do Gemini 4 Hydrogen aos do Claude Sonnet 5.5 e do GPT-6.1 Terra , dois modelos de nível intermediário. Segundo os resultados apresentados pela empresa, a IA do Google supera os concorrentes na maioria dos testes, mas perde para o modelo da Anthropic nas avaliações de programação agêntica (Terminal-Bench 4.1), uso do computador (OSWorld-2.1) e matemática e ciências (Termina-Bench-Science 0.1). Segundo o Google, o novo modelo representa um salto significativo em inteligência e velocidade em relação ao Gemini 3.8 Flash , seu antecessor de nível intermediário. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen executa tarefas 2,5 vezes mais rápido em sua configuração de esforço alto e alcançou mais do que o triplo da pontuação no Terminal-Bench 4.1 (57% contra 18,2%), quando comparado ao modelo anterior. O Gemini 4 Hydrogen pode ser acessado em diferentes canais do ecossistema Google . Para desenvolvedores, o modelo está disponível na API Gemini, no Android Studio e no AI Studio. Os assinantes dos planos Google AI Pro e AI Ultra também podem utilizá-lo no Google Antigravity. Quanto aos preços, o Gemini 4 Hydrogen cobra US$ 1,50 (R$ 8,46, em conversão direta) por milhão de tokens de entrada e US$ 7,50 (R$ 42,29) por milhão de tokens de saída. Para usuários gratuitos e assinantes do Google AI Plus, o modelo pode ser acessado no aplicativo Gemini e na Busca. Vale lembrar que, a partir desta sexta-feira (13), os assinantes do plano AI Plus não poderão mais selecionar modelos da categoria Gemini Pro . stories.summary: La compañía pide disculpas por el “problema técnico” y descarta que haya un ciberataque o agentes de IA detrás de los fallos que han tumbado el correo electrónico Outlook, la plataforma Teams o Copilot. No se han notificado incidencias reseñables en España

sources.name: El País Tecnología
sources.title: Los servicios de Microsoft retoman la normalidad tras una caída global de más de 18 horas
sources.text: La compañía pide disculpas por el “problema técnico” y descarta que haya un ciberataque o agentes de IA detrás de los fallos que han tumbado el correo electrónico Outlook, la plataforma Teams o Copilot. No se han notificado incidencias reseñables en España Microsoft ha informado este viernes en torno a las dos del mediodía, hora peninsular española, de que ya estaba recuperándose de la caída global de sus servicios que se inició en la tarde del jueves y que ha afectado a millones de usuarios de al menos 70 países. A partir de ese momento, la situación ha ido mejorando con el paso de las horas. “Estamos viendo un progreso continuo en la recuperación en las regiones afectadas, con mejoras más amplias en Norteamérica, mejoras sostenidas en gran parte de Europa y señales alentadoras de recuperación en Asia-Pacífico”, lee un comunicado de la compañía. En un mensaje en la red social X, la compañía añadió: “Lamentamos profundamente las interrupciones que este incidente ha causado a nuestros clientes y socios. Somos conscientes de la confianza que depositan en nuestros servicios y nos tomamos esa responsabilidad muy en serio. Se trató de un problema técnico, sin relación alguna con ciberataques, inteligencia artificial o agentes autónomos. El incidente tuvo su origen en un fallo durante una ampliación previa de la capacidad de la red, el cual se manifestó a raíz de una modificación reciente en la misma. Hemos resuelto el problema subyacente y continuamos restableciendo el servicio para los clientes y regiones restantes”. We are deeply sorry for the disruption this incident has caused our customers and partners. We know the trust they place in our services and take that responsibility extremely seriously. We are seeing broad recovery and stability across our services. This was a technical issue… Los productos afectados son el correo electrónico Outlook, el entorno Teams, SharePoint Online, el chatbot de inteligencia artificial (IA) Copilot, los servicios en la nube OneDrive y OneNote y el paquete Microsoft 365, que incluye aplicaciones como Word, Excel o PowerPoint. Se trata de programas muy presentes en los entornos corporativos, que canalizan grandes flujos de trabajo en oficinas tanto del sector privado como del público. “Por ahora, puedo confirmar que no hay indicios de que esto sea el resultado de una actividad maliciosa o cibernética”, ha escrito en X Lamanna, quien ocupa el cargo de vicepresidente de Copilot, Agentes y Plataformas de Microsoft, considerada la mayor empresa de software del mundo. La compañía ha asegurado esta tarde que, aunque las colas de correo electrónico se han “reducido significativamente, acercándose a niveles normales”, mientras continúa la recuperación de los sistemas, “algunos usuarios pueden experimentar problemas intermitentes de acceso o retrasos en la entrega de correos electrónicos”. “Sabemos que nuestros clientes dependen de nuestros servicios para realizar trabajos importantes todos los días, y lamentamos el impacto que estos cortes tuvieron en aquellos que dependen de nosotros”, han añadido posteriormente. We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue. We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity. Según la empresa, el problema no se debe a un aumento inesperado del tráfico por mayor actividad de los usuarios, sino a que varios servidores habían dejado de estar disponibles sin que eso se esperase y su trabajo recayó sobre los que quedaban, en un efecto dominó que terminó por saturar los sistemas. No hay todavía un análisis definitivo de por qué ha pasado eso, pero lo único que parece claro es que el problema afecta a los servicios “que interactúan con Exchange Online y el correo”. Por eso arrastró a Teams, SharePoint, Copilot, asociados al correo, mientras que los que no dependen de Exchange siguen funcionando. “Lo que sabemos por ahora es que ayer hubo un aumento anormal de tráfico de red que, a priori , parece indicar un fallo técnico muy probablemente vinculado con gestión BGP y DNS [protocolos de enrutamiento de tráfico online y sistema de nombres de dominio]. No hay evidencia de ataque alguno”, explica David Arroyo Guardeño, científico titular del Grupo de Investigación en Ciberseguridad y Protección de la Privacidad (GICP) del CSIC. “Las implicaciones de esta caída son enormes en un amplio grueso de sectores industriales. Microsoft Outlook y, cada vez más Copilot, están muy presentes en un porcentaje muy amplio de nuestros servicios e infraestructura digital”, añade. Las quejas de los usuarios en la plataforma especializada Downdetector alcanzaron un primer pico pasadas las siete de la tarde del jueves, hora peninsular española, y se reportaron problemas en más de 70 países. Esta mañana, sobre las siete, ha comenzado una segunda oleada de incidencias, que ha duplicado en volumen la registrada en la tarde del jueves. Pasadas las cinco de la tarde, el nivel de incidencias se asemejaba al de un día normal. Australia amaneció este viernes con el incidente que en España se sufrió el jueves por la tarde. Ha provocado problemas en empresas, que han experimentado dificultades para comunicarse, gestionar pedidos o enviar facturas, y en organismos y servicios públicos, incluyendo la agencia tributaria australiana y algunos tribunales. La caída ha afectado también a la Policía Federal Australiana (AFP), la agencia de inteligencia ASIO y Service NSW, la plataforma del estado de Nueva Gales del Sur que permite realizar trámites como renovar permisos de conducir o gestionar matriculaciones. Por eso, las autoridades del país han activado una cláusula de su acuerdo de resiliencia digital con Microsoft para pedir que sus intereses reciban prioridad en la recuperación de los servicios afectados por la caída global de la tecnológica estadounidense. sources.name: Xataka
sources.title: Microsoft recupera Outlook más de 24 horas después: ya sabemos qué provocó la caída de sus servicios
sources.text: Poco más tarde de las 7 de la mañana, Microsoft 365 Status ponía punto y final a una de las caídas más largas y pronunciadas de la historia de la informática moderna. Por fin habían restaurado el servicio completamente para todos los clientes y regiones afectadas tras abordar lo que causó este incidente que ha dejado sin Outlook, Teams, Copilot y el resto de Microsoft 365 durante más de un día, ya que los fallos empezaron durante la tarde del jueves en Estados Unidos , a las 17:17 horas de España. Una caída masiva y global . El fallo se traducía en una caída global que dejó sin acceso al correo electrónico y otras herramientas profesionales de su suite, como las videollamadas o su chatbot con IA. Según Downdetector, recibió avisos de incidencias en 74 países, con un alcance que no solo no entiende de fronteras, sino tampoco de sector o tamaño: millones de empresas como la gigante Maersk en la logística , administraciones públicas como la Junta de Andalucía , así como hospitales como los del servicio nacional de salud del Reino Unido , las autoridades como en Los Angeles o hasta la prestigiosa universidad de Stanford sufrieron en sus carnes la incidencia. Por qué ha ocurrido . Horas antes de anunciar el restablecimiento completo, Microsoft se disculpaba públicamente en su perfil de y daba una explicación oficial a lo sucedido: el problema comenzó durante una actualización anterior de la capacidad de su red. Pero el fallo no apareció en ese momento, sino cuando la empresa ejecutó un cambio posterior en esa infraestructura. En el mensaje descartan además que la incidencia estuviera relacionada con la ciberseguridad o ataques IA. En cualquier caso, han prometido un informe completo del incidente al concluir la revisión. Sabíamos que el origen del fallo eran los servidores de Exchange Online, pero no por qué: primero hablaban de una "carga elevada” en varias regiones , luego de que muchos servidores se habían quedado fuera de servicio inesperadamente, más tarde apuntaban a fallos en las comprobaciones de salud automáticas , aunque esa hipótesis duró poco. Poco después, Microsoft empezó a revertir un cambio en la configuración de la red , precisamente la explicación oficial que ha dado la empresa fundada por Gates y Allen. Recuperación gradual . Una de las razones por las que la caída ha sido tan larga es cómo Microsoft ha recuperado los servicios. En el mensaje, la compañía detalla que han solucionado el problema de fondo y que han optado por un restablecimiento progresivo. Así, ha explicado que considerando la magnitud de la demanda, han ido restaurando los servicios gradualmente, validando en cada etapa que la infraestructura funcionara correctamente. Microsoft reconoce que este procedimiento ha prolongado la recuperación, pero lo ha considerado necesario para garantizar un restablecimiento estable. Cronología de la caída y la recuperación . Así ha ido evolucionando la avería de Microsoft, en hora peninsular española (CET): Pocas empresas con mucho poder . La caída pone de manifiesto hasta qué punto dependen particulares, empresas y administradores de escasos proveedores tecnológicos para tareas esenciales para su desempeño profesional. El problema no es solo no recibir un correo o no poder tener una reunión, es que cuando infraestructuras tan colosales falla, medio mundo se para: trámites administrativos que no pueden llevarse a cabo, comunicaciones internas o servicios críticos. De hecho y como recoge Reuters , hubo quien tuvo que recurrir al fax. El problema de las últimas horas es en realidad un déjá vú de la dependencia tecnológica concentrada: el fallo de ClowdStrike sobre Azure dejó a hospitales y pymes fuera de juego hace un par de años o cómo hace aproximadamente un año un fallo en AWS dejó sin internet a medio mundo . Según la Comisión Europea , Amazon con AWS, Microsoft con Azure y Google Cloud concentran más del 70% del mercado europeo. El de ayer fue una (otra) muestra más. sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Nvidia board urged to consider 'potential return of Jensen Huang' by two major investors
sources.text: Two major Nvidia shareholders are calling on the board of directors to weigh all options for the company's future leadership, including "the potential return of Jensen Huang." Altimeter Capital CEO Brad Gerstner posted a letter on X on Friday that urges Nvidia's board to "pursue a slow, measured, and deliberate process regarding the future leadership of Nvidia." The letter is also signed by Atreides Management's Gavin Baker. Nvidia was Altimeter Capital's largest disclosed equity holding in its most recent SEC filing , with a 9.4 million-share stake worth nearly $1.9 billion as of June 30. Atreides held 1.2 million shares worth nearly $250 million at the end of June. The letter said Nvidia will be "capably led" by interim CEO Colette Kress , who served as Nvidia's CFO for 13 years before the board announced Thursday that she'd lead the company in Huang's absence. "But the Founder and long time incredible leader of this extraordinary company has earned the right for a deliberate process that avoids any needless rush to replace him before all the facts are known," the letter concludes. The document did not call for Huang's immediate reinstatement. Nvidia founder Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday amid multiple affair allegations, including one with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang , who also worked with Nvidia customer Megaspeed . The Singapore-based company is being investigated by the Justice Department for possibly redirecting some of its supply of Nvidia's restricted artificial intelligence chips to China. SpaceX CEO Elon Musk said on X Friday that he signed a petition asking to reinstate Huang. A petition circulating online called "Stand with Jensen" claims to have more than 100,000 signatures, including more than 5,000 current Nvidia employees. Musk said on X Saturday that without Huang, some "critical deals will be lost." Another letter sent Friday called on U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick to testify about Megaspeed before the House Intelligence Committee. Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10 about whether the Commerce Department is "properly performing its broader role of preventing China from acquiring advanced AI chips," according to the letter. Huang has also been asked to testify . The Commerce Department originally launched an investigation into Megaspeed that was moved to the Justice Department in 2025 after Nvidia's lawyer contacted a senior Commerce official, according to The New York Times. President Donald Trump is scheduled to visit China on Thursday, but doesn't plan to raise Nvidia and the suspected spy affair during his meeting with Chinese president Xi Jinping , according to U.S. officials. Musk is expected to join Trump on the trip to Shenzhen, China, for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit on Nov. 18 and 19.

sources.title: ¿Quiénes son los principales candidatos a reemplazar a Jensen Huang en NVIDIA?
sources.text: Con la renuncia de Jensen Huang todavía fresca , el desenlace del drama que hoy envuelve a NVIDIA todavía es un misterio. La empresa busca dar vuelta la página tras el nombramiento de Colette Kress como CEO interina, pensando en la presentación de resultados financieros que concretará el próximo 17 de noviembre. La jefa de finanzas, devenida temporalmente en consejera delegada, tendrá la difícil misión de poner la cara ante los accionistas e inversores en una sesión que seguramente estará repleta de preguntas incómodas. Y es un hecho que en su gran mayoría no estarán vinculadas con el desempeño comercial de la empresa, pues analistas de Wall Street estiman que las cifras de ventas del trimestre duplicará a las del período previo. Las infidelidades de Jensen Huang, incluida una con una supuesta espía china , serán la comidilla del evento. También, los reportes de un sistema de gestión ejecutiva feudal y las ramificaciones del escrutinio regulatorio que muy posiblemente le caerá a la compañía en el futuro inmediato. Todas cuestiones que ni siquiera se discutirían de no ser porque el CEO de NVIDIA se envalentonó con volar demasiado cerca del sol . NVIDIA ha puesto en marcha un procedimiento para seleccionar al reemplazo definitivo de Jensen Huang . La compañía dice que va a explorar candidatos internos y externos, aunque por lo pronto se desconoce cuánto tiempo le demandará esta tarea. Tampoco se sabe si la junta prefiere ascender a un ejecutivo ya conocido, o si la balanza se inclina más hacia alguien de afuera. Un reporte de Bloomberg sobre los últimos días de Jensen Huang en NVIDIA menciona dos nombres en particular que destacan . Si bien no serían los únicos en consideración, la publicación afirma que tienen grandes posibilidades de quedar en la lista corta final. Por un lado, se habla de Lisa Su , la CEO de AMD . En cierto modo, podría ser la indicada para el cargo, considerando su vasta experiencia en roles de este tipo, su gran conocimiento técnico y el aval de haber liderado la etapa de mayor crecimiento de la compañía. Cuando asumió en 2014, AMD valía unos 3.000 millones de dólares. Hoy en día, la capitalización bursátil ronda los 860.000 millones, y unos pocos meses atrás llegó a superar 1 billón de dólares. Lisa Su es una figura muy respetada en el mundo de la tecnología y podría ser la pieza justa para NVIDIA. Lo curioso es que comparte un parentesco con Jensen Huang por parte de su madre. Dicho todo esto, suena complejo pensar que la jefa de AMD pueda "cambiar de bando" para asumir el control del gigante verde. El otro nombre que estaría entre los candidatos principales es el de Rene Haas , CEO de ARM . Dicha empresa es la que se encarga de diseñar la arquitectura en la que se basan una gran cantidad de chips para ordenadores, dispositivos móviles, servidores, placas gráficas, coches y relojes inteligentes, y mucho más. Algunas de las empresas que utilizan tecnología desarrollada por ARM son NVIDIA, Apple, Qualcomm, Samsung, Broadcom, Amazon y Texas Instruments. Si Rene Haas reemplaza a Jensen Huang como CEO de NVIDIA, será un giro peculiar de los eventos. Recordemos que la empresa californiana quiso comprar ARM en 2020 , pero finalmente abandonó ese intento en 2022 tras frenos regulatorios y quejas de rivales. Vale aclarar, no obstante, que esto fue cuando Simon Segars era jefe de la firma británica. Pase lo que pase, la elección del sucesor de Jensen Huang seguirá dando que hablar. Hasta Donald Trump ha sugerido a Tim Cook como candidato, pues opina que es el único capaz de liderar NVIDIA y mantenerla en el top mundial.

sources.title: Pay for Hugging Face Hub with your Google Cloud Account
sources.text: You can now link your Hugging Face organization to your Google Cloud account, so that your Hugging Face usage shows up on your Google Cloud bill instead of being charged to a credit card. Get started on the Google Cloud Marketplace . Hugging Face is where teams find, build and run open models: from hosting private models and datasets, to running GPU workloads with Jobs , deploying models with Inference Endpoints , calling thousands of models through Inference Providers , or hosting demos on GPU Spaces . If your company already runs on Google Cloud, adding a new vendor and a corporate credit card just to use these services can slow things down. By linking your organization through the Google Cloud Marketplace: If you're an admin of your Hugging Face organization, here's how to set it up, step by step. Go to the Hugging Face Hub listing on the Google Cloud Marketplace, select the Google Cloud project you want to use, and click on "Subscribe". You are now on the subscription page. Select the billing account to be charged, review and accept the terms, then click "Subscribe". Once the order is placed, Google Cloud asks you to finish setting up your account with Hugging Face. Click on "Sign up with Hugging Face" to be redirected to Hugging Face. You are now on Hugging Face, where you can select the organization you want to link to your Google Cloud account. Only organizations where you are an admin are listed. Select it and confirm. You are then redirected to the billing settings of your organization. The payment method section now shows the linked Google Cloud account, with a pending status. Every cloud marketplace subscription is reviewed by the Hugging Face team before paid usage starts being billed through it. While the subscription is pending, usage keeps being billed to the organization's existing payment method, if any. Once your subscription is approved, you will receive an email confirming that your Google Cloud account and Hugging Face organization are linked. Organizations that already have a credit card on file switch to cloud marketplace billing at the start of their next billing period. Organizations on the free tier with no credit card on file usually switch immediately, so their paid usage is billed through the cloud marketplace right away. To confirm it, open the billing settings of your organization : the Google Cloud account is now shown as the organization's active payment method. Your organization is now billed through your Google Cloud account. All members of your organization can use Hugging Face compute services, and the usage will show up on your Google Cloud bill. Thanks for reading! You can find more details in the billing documentation . If you have any questions, please contact us at billing@huggingface.co .

sources.title: Decision Models in Hugging Face
sources.text: Large Language Models (LLMs) are exceptionally good at generating text. We use them to answer questions, write code, reason about problems, and so much more. But not every problem requires generating text. Consider a customer support system receiving the following message: "I was charged twice for my subscription. I need a refund today." The system needs to determine which team should handle the request, how urgent it is, and whether the customer is requesting a refund. We could ask an LLM to return a JSON object containing these answers. But what if the model could directly evaluate the available options and return a probability distribution over them, without generating any text ? This is the key idea behind decision models . A decision model takes some input context (state), evaluates a question with a set of predefined possible answers (primitives), and returns a structured decision along with probabilities. Instead of asking a model to generate an answer token by token, we ask it to assign probabilities to the answers that our application already understands. TypeSafe AI introduced Jev , describing it as a System One model . The name draws inspiration from the distinction between fast, intuitive thinking (System 1) and slower, deliberative thinking (System 2). The community has converged to the term decision model , because it describes the model's computational role rather than invoking a particular theory of cognition. In the rest of the post we will refer to the models as "decision models" instead of "system one models". ( A poll on twitter deciding what we should be calling such models ) For a decision model, the fundamental interface is: We could simply prompt an LLM to return a JSON object containing our decisions. In fact, this is how many applications already use language models for classification, routing, and other structured tasks. However, there are a few problems with this approach. Before understanding the interface of a decision model, it is useful to revisit two closely related approaches namely traditional classification and zero-shot classification. Suppose we train a classifier that routes customer-support requests to three departments: A conventional classification model learns a mapping from an input to a predefined set of labels. During training, the model learns to predict these labels from examples. A classification head typically produces one logit per class, and softmax turns those logits into a probability distribution. The limitation here is that the output classes are baked into the model's classification head . If we introduce a fourth department, such as Legal, the existing classifier does not automatically acquire a corresponding output class. We may need to modify the head, collect training data, and retrain or adapt the model. Zero-shot classification addresses an important part of this limitation. Instead of requiring the classifier to be trained specifically on every output category, we supply the candidate labels at inference time. Unlike a conventional fixed-label classifier, the categories can change from one request to another. Let’s add another department, such as “Legal”, and see the model outputs. One common implementation uses a model trained for natural language inference (NLI). Each candidate label is converted into a hypothesis, and the model measures how strongly the input entails that hypothesis. This already sounds quite similar to a decision model. And in many ways, it is. Decision models extend this idea beyond simply assigning an input to a category. A decision model can accept several named questions about the same state, with different answer types. The types can be choosing between alternatives (choice), scoring an ordered scale (score), or estimating the probability that a statement is true (noul). More importantly, its interface is designed around the probability distribution over possible decisions . The advantage of decision models is not that they invented runtime-defined labels or probabilistic classification. It is that they organize these capabilities into a consistent interface, potentially backed by architectures and training procedures optimized specifically for decisions. A decision model request has the following two components: The state is the information the model should evaluate. It may be a string, a structured JSON object, or, other modalities for supported omni-modal models. Questions describe what we want to know about the state. In the decision models interface, three fundamental primitives represent different forms of decisions: Choice is the most intuitive primitive and the closest to traditional classification. Which department should handle this customer request? The available options are Billing, Technical support, and Sales. The model assigns a logit to each option.
